title: Staged KV-cache quantization profiles + drift analysis for INT8/FP8 rollout
creator: Maya Patel
description: Objective: evaluate staged quantization profiles for the KV cache (INT8 and FP8) and define a safe calibration+rollout workflow that balances latency SLOs with negligible quality regression. This ticket covers (1) calibration dataset curation and windowing, (2) staged profile generation (per-layer + conservative hybrid fallbacks), (3) synthetic and real drift injection, (4) canary rollout policy and monitoring thresholds. We want a reproducible pipeline that outputs profiles + conservative fallback heuristics and a recommended rollout recipe for ops teams.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Calibration pipeline that produces per-layer quant profiles for INT8 and FP8 and stores metadata; 2) Reproducible evaluation harness comparing FP16 vs INT8 vs FP8 on our eval corpus with p50/p95 latency, tokens/s, and quality deltas recorded; 3) Drift-detection test that flags >0.8 KL divergence on KV distributions and triggers profile re-calibration; 4) Runbook + canary config that limits initial traffic to 5% with automatic rollback on >0.5% top-N quality regression or >10% p95 latency regression; 5) PRs merging code and dashboards.
experiment_plan: - Step 1: Assemble calibration datasets: 50k prompt traces stratified by sequence length (short/medium/long), plus a held-out production sample (10k). - Step 2: Implement staged profile generator: (A) conservative per-layer symmetric INT8, (B) per-layer asymmetric INT8, (C) e4m3 FP8 profile, (D) hybrid profile that uses FP8 for attention KV and INT8 for FFN cache. Profiles stored with metadata: seq_len distribution, calibration window, timestamp. - Step 3: Baseline runs on dedicated test cluster (A100/80GB equivalent) measuring p50/p95 token latency and tokens/sec for batch sizes {1,4,8} and typical request seq lengths. - Step 4: Inject synthetic drift: scale activations by +10% and +25% on attention KV to simulate domain shift; re-evaluate quality metrics. - Step 5: Canary rollout: 5% traffic -> 20% -> 50% with monitoring gates. - Step 6: Post-mortem and recommendations for ops (fallback heuristics, auto-recalibration cadence).
results_summary: Preliminary runs on decoupled testbed (seq_len distribution: 32/256/1024) show: INT8 (per-layer asymmetric) reduced median token latency by ~28% vs FP16 for batch=1, p95 improved by ~18%, but averaged QA EM dropped by 0.7% on the long-seq subset. FP8 (e4m3) reduced median latency by ~22% with a smaller QA EM drop (~0.35%). Hybrid profile (FP8 for KV, INT8 for FFN-cache) hit a middle ground: ~25% latency reduction and ~0.4% QA EM delta. Under +25% synthetic drift, INT8 showed increased variance in log-prob deltas and a 1.6x higher KL shift compared to FP8. These suggest FP8 is more robust under distributional shift while INT8 yields larger tail latency improvements. All numbers are preliminary and require repeat runs across hardware variants.
tech_notes: - Calibration window: 2k sequences sampled over last 7 days for production re-calibration; for initial experiments we used 50k curated sequences. - Per-layer scale clipping used for INT8 asymmetric; tested both max-based and percentile(99.9) clipping. Percentile clipping reduced outlier-driven quantization error. - FP8 profiles used e4m3 format with dynamic exponent bias adjustment where available. - Implemented lightweight KV distribution histogram export hook to S3 for drift detection. - Observed that KV cache layout (interleaved vs contiguous) affects kernel selection and therefore measured latency; profiling must run on identical container images as production.
observations_and_tradeoffs: - Latency vs quality: INT8 best for raw latency but more sensitive to unseen activation shifts; FP8 offers robust quality with slightly less latency win. - Calibration cadence: frequent lightweight recalibration with percentile clipping mitigates drift without full retraining of profiles. - Rollout safety: conservative hybrid fallback (if KL>threshold or p95 latency regresses) must be implemented before 100% promotion. - Ops complexity: hybrid profiles add complexity to serving runtime (per-operator profile selection) but reduce need for immediate rollback under drift.
next_steps: 1) Run 5 deterministic repeats on three hardware families (A100, H100, RTX8000) and aggregate stats. 2) Implement automated KL-based drift gate: if KV histogram KL > 0.8 relative to calibration baseline, trigger canary pause and schedule re-calibration job. 3) Build a dashboards template (cost/latency/quality) and a playbook for SREs. 4) Draft PR for canary config and emergency rollback lambda. 5) Coordinate with product to identify two low-risk customer clusters for supervised canary trials.
